title: proactive-nccl-stream-fusing-and-kvcache-coalescer-for-tp-overlap
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Multi-GPU tensor-parallel workloads at high concurrency show recurring stalls where asynchronous NCCL work and kernel launches fail to overlap because short-lived communication streams are created and torn down frequently and small KV cache writes become a scheduling pressure point. This PR implements two coordinated runtime optimizations: (1) proactive NCCL stream fusing to reduce stream churn and allow larger batched progress of comm operations, and (2) a KVCache coalescer that batches small KV write/update operations and applies them on the host in a latency-aware micro-batch window. Together these reduce comm/compute handshake stalls and smooth kernel scheduler load to improve throughput and tail latency.
description_details: Design summary: The proactive NCCL stream fuser maintains a warm pool of persistent NCCL streams with light-weight affinity tagging (per-tensor-shard + priority level). Instead of spawning ephemeral streams for each collective, the runtime reuses fused streams and aggregates small collectives into a single multi-chunk enqueue when affinity/ordering permits. The KVCache coalescer operates at the request-aggregation layer: small KV updates from token-level requests are buffered for up to X micros (adaptive based on observed inter-arrival) and flushed in a single host->device memcpy and kv-apply kernel. The coalescer respects strict ordering for cache line conflicts and falls back to immediate applies for critical low-latency requests.
implementation_notes:
- Added nccl/stream_pool.{h,cpp} implementing persistent stream pools and a lightweight fused-enqueue API.
- Extended tp/scheduler to expose stream affinity hints and mergeable-collective predicates.
- New kvcache/coalescer.{h,cpp} with host side buffers, conflict detection, and a small state machine for flush policy.
- Metric hooks and trace points added: fused_stream_count, kvcache_coalesce_rate, coalesce_flush_latency, comm_compute_gap_ms.
- Unit tests for stream_pool concurrency, and integration tests in perf-canary harness.
- Backwards compatibility: default behavior disabled behind runtime flag rwn.tp.proactive_fuse=false; coalescer gated by rwn.kvcache.coalesce=true.
performance_summary: Perf (internal perf-canary runs, 8xA100, fp16, typical prompt mix): median throughput +13% vs baseline; 95th-percentile token latency -7%; end-to-end cost per token estimated -9% under production microbatch patterns. Stress runs (high small-request fraction) show up to 24% reduction in comm stalls and 30% lower variance in per-step scheduling latency.

Marta Ivanova (approver): Verified perf numbers in canary and reviewed safety fallback. Approving for merge.
rollout_plan: Feature gated; enable on canary clusters for 48h, measure fused_stream_count and coalesce_flush_latency; then staged rollout to dedicated pools by percentage (10%, 30%, 100%) with automated rollback on >5% increase in 95p latency or >2% increase in error rate.
rollback_strategy: Runtime flags allow immediate disable; CI/CD job to patch runtime flags across fleets. If persistent regressions observed, revert using rollback branch rb/99501-revert which removes fused enqueue hooks and coalescer registration.
release_notes: Runtime: Added optional proactive NCCL stream fusing and KV cache coalescer to reduce comm/compute stalls in tensor-parallel workloads. Behind feature flags and disabled by default for private installs. Expected throughput improvements for small-request-heavy workloads.
notes_for_ops: Metrics to watch: fused_stream_count (should increase), kvcache_coalesce_rate (should be non-zero for small-request traffic), coalesce_flush_latency (p95 < configured window). If p95 latency spikes, disable rwn.tp.proactive_fuse and rwn.kvcache.coalesce and contact runtime-oncall.
audits: security: no new network surfaces; coalescer buffers are host-only and bounds-checked
compliance: feature disabled in private installer by default, documented in docs/ops/rollout-notes/
